title: 本地看板读取 API 与进程边界
status_note: The audit findings P1-1..P1-3 and P2-1..P2-16 are fixed or explicitly documented, each with an executable verification. Batch reconnection is still the integration owner's step; this record accepts the module, not the batch.
record_commit: the commit containing this record file
worktree_note: Recorded with ~ for the user home because the frozen contract privacy validator rejects absolute home-directory paths inside plans/; the absolute path stays in the execution session.
batch_state: batch 6 is open; this module opens no PR, merges nothing and publishes nothing
evidence_tree: clean checkout of 198aeb1 after `python scripts/dev.py setup-node` (or an equivalent src/thu_assistant/node_modules link); dev.py test needs the tough-cookie runtime dependency
outputs: exactly the seven frozen routes plus an optional static shell: /api/v1/health, /services, /services/{service_id}, /query/{service_id}/{operation}, /todos, /calendar, /resources; no prepare, execute, payment, upload, model, key or config route exists
GET and HEAD only; every other method returns 405 with Allow: GET, HEAD before the facade is reached; GET/HEAD bodies are refused and above 64 KiB is 413
loopback binding only: 0.0.0.0, ::, localhost and any external address are refused before a socket opens; port 0 gives an ephemeral port and an explicit port is honoured

Host header exact allowlist with the bound port; Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site checks run before both API and static routes, so a cross-site page cannot read JSON or static assets; no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is ever emitted

process-bound sessions: a single-use 0600 bootstrap file plus X-Openthu-Bootstrap for automated clients, and a trusted loopback navigation for the browser shell; the token never enters a URL, a log line or the shared configuration and is deleted after one exchange

session cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, without Domain and with a bounded Max-Age; Secure is deliberately not set because some browsers drop it on loopback HTTP; ids are stored only as SHA-256 digests
session capacity never evicts an active session: a full store returns LOCAL_API_SESSION_LIMIT and the browser keeps its cookie; duplicate same-name cookies from another loopback port are all verified
bootstrap reads use O_NOFOLLOW plus fstat and a bounded read from one descriptor; a symlink, a non-regular file, a loose mode or a foreign owner is rejected

per-session sliding-window rate limit (120 requests / 10 s) with a local code and local text; a 10 s minimum interval for an identical expensive read is committed only after a non-5xx response, and HEAD or a cursor resume does not consume it
request bounds: 2048-character path, 8192-character query, 4096-character parameters object, ASCII-only page_size 1..200 with default 50; duplicate or unknown query parameters are rejected

parameters accept only a bounded JSON object with safe keys; url/uri/href/method/headers/endpoint/target/destination/source/origin/address/return_url and similar keys are rejected; NaN/Infinity literals are rejected before the facade
path traversal, encoded dot segments, backslashes, NULs and double slashes are rejected before routing; static assets resolve under the configured directory and a symlink escape is not served

local paging slices a facade page larger than page_size, mints an opaque lac1 cursor bound to session, route, parameters and page size, expires it after 600 s and carries a trailing facade cursor forward on the last slice; caps are aligned with the 8 MiB response ceiling

two executor pools: health/services/detail use a two-worker priority pool; expensive reads use eight workers whose capacity is held by the worker, so eight stuck adapters cannot block health and the next read fails fast with LOCAL_API_BUSY

per-request deadline (default 30 s) with cooperative cancellation; a timed-out source returns 504/TIMEOUT while other cards keep serving, and stop() cancels this instance's tokens and closes its socket in bounded time

facade envelopes are checked against every declared result-envelope-v1 property (types, enums, lengths, items array, snapshot_complete, missing_pages, source_errors, error object, finite numbers); an invalid optional field is 502 LOCAL_API_FACADE_INVALID_RESPONSE, never a 200/READY

the envelope source.service_id/operation must equal the requested route (query exact, todos agenda/todos, calendar agenda/calendar, resources resources/resources), so a mis-routed adapter cannot paint another service's data on a card
a facade without a method returns 501 LOCAL_API_FACADE_UNAVAILABLE, not a 500 or a fabricated empty result

display projection drops exact credential/member/private-path keys and credential-shaped key segments (cookie_header, csrf_token_value, auth, *_header, *_api_key); it redacts home/Windows/temp paths and token shapes, caps text and depth, and replaces non-finite numbers

links are filtered in string, array and mapping shapes for links/link/*_url/*_link/*_href; only https tsinghua.edu.cn without a CAS/SSO/login/ticket marker survives, arrays keep their length with null entries, and withheld paths are reported as LOCAL_API_LINK_WITHHELD_AT:<path>

every response is a result-envelope-v1 object carrying request_id, display.state, display.message, display.next_step, display.completeness, display.provenance and display.paging; the encoded body is capped at max_response_bytes (8 MiB) and a larger body becomes 502 LOCAL_API_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE
AUTH_REQUIRED from a campus source stays HTTP 200 with display.state LOGIN_REQUIRED and a next step pointing to the existing controlled entry; the local API never retries a campus login

static shell is optional and served only from the configured directory with an allowlisted content type, no-store, CSP and X-Frame-Options; without it the API still runs and / returns LOCAL_API_UI_NOT_INSTALLED
serve(host, port, facade, ...) is exported for the 6.1 CLI dashboard command and maps localhost to 127.0.0.1; no subprocess, signal, os.kill or outbound HTTP import exists in the module

32 LOCAL_API_* error codes are registered in error-classification-v1 and mirrored in source_state; the block sits at the head of both registries so a batch merge with 6.1 has no conflict and keeps the union

limits: The real 6.1 facade adapter is still the batch integration step. 6.2 now requires all seven methods (health, services, query, describe, todos, calendar, resources), exact source.service_id/operation, a declared cancel parameter and bounded upstream I/O; a missing method is 501 LOCAL_API_FACADE_UNAVAILABLE, not a fabricated result.

local-read-api-v1 declares next_cursor on /todos, /calendar and /resources but omits the request field. The server accepts an opaque cursor on those routes as a documented extension; 1.1/8.1 must revise the frozen contract or drop paging there.

The static shell is only a seam: 6.2 serves an optional static_dir and owns no HTML. 7.1 owns src/thu_assistant/web_assets and must pass it; without it / returns LOCAL_API_UI_NOT_INSTALLED while the JSON API keeps working.

Bootstrap tokens are single-use and their file is deleted on exchange. A session that expires later requires restarting the local instance to obtain a new token; the browser navigation path is unaffected. This is the cost of removing the replayable 300-second token.

The browser session bootstrap trusts a loopback navigation with Sec-Fetch-Site none/same-origin; another process of the same OS account is treated as trusted because it can already read the profile, while remote pages are blocked by Host, Origin and fetch metadata.
Secure is not set on the session cookie because some browsers refuse it over http://127.0.0.1. Protection is the loopback-only bind plus Host/Origin checks; a future TLS front end must add Secure.
No non-read route exists, so the CSRF helper is tested but unused. Any future refresh or write route must require both an allowed origin and the CSRF token before doing work.

Rate limits are engineering bounds: 120 requests / 10 s per session, a 10 s interval for an identical expensive read, and a fast LOCAL_API_BUSY when all eight read slots are held. HEAD performs one facade read (same metadata semantics as GET) but does not consume the refresh slot and remains subject to the per-session limit.

A non-cooperative adapter thread cannot be killed in-process. Health/services stay available, expensive reads fail fast and stop() returns, but Python joins executor threads at interpreter exit, so 6.1 must bound its HTTP timeouts; a permanently blocked adapter can still delay process exit.
Bootstrap mode/owner checks and O_NOFOLLOW are POSIX-only; on Windows the explicit symlink check is used and the file stays under the per-user state directory, but the 0600 assertion is skipped.

Display projection is not a general DLP. It drops exact and credential-shaped keys (auth_state is intentionally dropped) and redacts known token/path shapes, but adapters must still keep raw credentials, member values and private paths out of envelopes.

The response ceiling is 8 MiB and the local paging store shares it; a larger facade page becomes 502 LOCAL_API_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE instead of a truncated success. A correct facade should page at the source.

One earlier full-suite attempt hit tests/test_action_framework.py::test_concurrent_execute_dispatches_once with STATE_READ_FAILED. It is a 4.4-owned concurrency race, touches no 6.2 code and did not reproduce in the audit or the final two full runs; it stays visible for 4.4/8.1.

The error-registry block was moved to the head of both files. `git merge-tree` against hermes/6.1 reports zero conflicts in the error registries and 359 union codes. Because 6.2's acceptance also updates the shared delivery ledgers, the full tree has five expected ledger-status conflicts (the 6.1/6.2 rows and the 17/17 counts); the integrator resolves them by union (18 accepted / 6 pending) and reruns both contract validators rather than choosing one side.
This module was verified with synthetic facades and loopback HTTP only. No real campus account, source, model or browser was used, and no booking, submission or payment exists in the route table.

There is no store or schema migration. Remove leftover <state>/local-api/bootstrap-*.json files from a crashed instance; sessions are memory-only and expire with the process. MCP, CLI, campus adapters and the dashboard assets are untouched.
